issues.legal_issue: Different treatment of persons transferring assets to Pakistan in distinct historical periods does not violate equal protection when the groups are not similarly situated and the difference in benefits does not arise directly from the challenged provision.
material_facts: The challenged provision concerned persons declared to be intending evacuees after transferring assets to Pakistan between the two specified historical dates.
A separate statutory category covered persons who transferred assets to Pakistan after the later date.
The latter category could seek restoration of property and compensation, benefits unavailable to persons declared to be intending evacuees under the earlier-period provision.

The periods followed different political conditions, and the difference in restoration and compensation benefits resulted from the legislature’s omission to extend those benefits to intending evacuees, rather than directly from the challenged provision.
issues.conclusion: The two groups were not similarly circumstanced, so denying them equal benefits did not infringe the constitutional guarantee of equal protection; the challenged provision was not invalid on this ground.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 does not require identical treatment of groups that are not similarly circumstanced. The Court considered the distinction between transfers made in the two periods, the relevant provisions of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, including sections 2(d)(iv), 16 and 22(b), and section 13 of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954. It held that the differing benefits arose from the legislature’s omission to extend benefits to the earlier-period group, not directly from section 22(b). No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: equal_protection_challenge and distinct_transfer_period_groups and benefits_differed_between_groups and historical_conditions_differed and benefit_difference_not_created_by_challenged_rule

predicates.equal_protection_challenge: A person challenged a legal distinction between groups as denying equal protection.
predicates.distinct_transfer_period_groups: The groups transferred assets to another country during different historical periods.
predicates.benefits_differed_between_groups: One group could obtain restoration or compensation benefits that were unavailable to the other group.
predicates.historical_conditions_differed: The historical and political conditions surrounding the two periods differed.
predicates.benefit_difference_not_created_by_challe: The difference in benefits resulted from other legislative provisions or omissions rather than directly from the challenged rule.

issues.definition: When an equal-protection challenge concerns groups distinguished by transfer periods, and their circumstances differed while the benefit difference arose outside the challenged rule, the different treatment does not violate equal protection.

issues.legal_issue: A substantial transfer of assets to Pakistan may support a declaration that property is evacuee property even when the transfer occurred before the person was declared an intending evacuee.
material_facts: The person was declared an intending evacuee after transferring a substantial portion of assets situated in India to Pakistan.
The transfer occurred before the declaration that the person was an intending evacuee.
The Custodian declared the person’s property to be evacuee property on the basis of that substantial transfer.
The statutory explanation treated a transfer of a substantial portion of assets as a circumstance constituting preparation for migration.
issues.conclusion: The transfer was available for consideration despite having occurred before the intending-evacuee declaration, and the property declaration was not improperly made on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: Section 22(b) of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, read with its explanation, permitted the Custodian to consider a substantial transfer of assets as a circumstance constituting preparation for migration. The statutory language required the circumstance to relate to a person declared to be an intending evacuee, but did not require the circumstance itself to arise after that declaration. Section 19 provided for the declaration of a person as an intending evacuee. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: property_declaration_appeal and person_declared_intending_evacuee and substantial_asset_transfer_to_another_country and transfer_preceded_intending_declaration

predicates.property_declaration_appeal: The proceeding challenges a declaration that a person’s property is evacuee property.
predicates.person_declared_intending_evacuee: The person whose property was declared evacuee property had been declared an intending evacuee.
predicates.substantial_asset_transfer_to_another_co: The person transferred a substantial portion of assets situated in the relevant territory to another country.
predicates.transfer_preceded_intending_declaration: The substantial asset transfer occurred before the person was declared an intending evacuee.

issues.definition: In an appeal concerning an evacuee-property declaration, a substantial transfer to another country made before the intending-evacuee declaration may support the property declaration.
